objective:
Think about how to grow the Swarm Pepe NFT collection, then propose five ideas.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verify all of it yourself before proposing anything:

  SwarmPepe ERC-721  0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb  Ethereum mainnet
  PixelArt renderer  0x07Fd9841eEB6a359EfB30f861D59bFa1f6B03FcA
  OpenSea            opensea.io/assets/ethereum/0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb
  X                  @swarmpepes
  The swarm itself   explorer.imd.fun, imd.fun/docs

Read the verified source of both contracts before you write a single idea. Call
tokenURI on a live token and look at what it actually returns. Check the current
totalMinted, how many are revealed, and the allowlist mechanics.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT, do not propose anything that violates it:

Both contracts are deployed and immutable. There is no proxy and no upgrade path.
The owner can do exactly four things: grant allowlist slots, open or close the
mint, change the royalty receiver, transfer ownership. Nothing else. MAX_SUPPLY
and MAX_PER_WALLET are constants. The renderer address is immutable.

So any idea that needs new contract behaviour means a SECOND contract that reads
the first one. Say so explicitly when that is what you mean, and explain what the
new contract would read and why the original stays untouched.

WHO IS EXECUTING

One person, no team, no budget worth mentioning, with access to this swarm.
An idea that needs a designer, a community manager or ten thousand dollars is
not an idea for this project. Say plainly which ideas need money and how much.

FOR EACH OF THE FIVE IDEAS, in this order:

  1. what it is, in two sentences
  2. what already exists that makes it possible, pointing at the specific
     contract function, event or API endpoint
  3. what has to be built, and whether that is a second contract, a page, a
     script, or nothing at all
  4. rough effort: hours, days or weeks, for one person with a swarm
  5. the one number that would tell us it worked, and how to read that number
     off chain or off a public API
  6. the strongest argument against doing it

Rank them. Put the one you would do first at the top and say why.

Then kill your own weakest idea: name which of the five you would drop entirely
if you could only keep four, and explain what is wrong with it. An answer that
defends all five equally is a failed answer.

PLUS ONE VIDEO IDEA, separate from the five

One concrete concept for a short video about the collection, 20 to 40 seconds.
Give a beat sheet with timings, what is on screen at each beat, and where the
visual assets come from. The art must come from the collection's own renderer
or from tokenURI, never invented. Say what makes this video different from a
generic NFT trailer, in one sentence.

RULES

Ground every claim in something you checked. If you did not verify it, say so.
No growth-hacking boilerplate, no "partner with influencers", no "build a
community", no roadmap language. Specific or nothing.
Do not propose anything that needs a person's real identity, wallet clustering
or deanonymisation.
State the block height for every on-chain number you quote.
